prompt: Implement KeyValueStore<K, V>, a small typed wrapper around a HashMap with put, get, getOrDefault, containsKey, size, and a removeIfValue method that deletes every entry holding a given value.
explanation: A class with two type parameters <K, V> passes them straight through to its private HashMap<K, V>, so callers get compile-time checking on both keys and values while the map itself stays hidden. Most methods simply delegate to the map. removeIfValue is the interesting one: the map's values() view is live, so map.values().removeIf(...) deletes the underlying entries -- a safe alternative to removing while iterating entrySet by hand.
hints: put, get, getOrDefault, containsKey and size can each delegate directly to the private map.
Removing from a map while looping over it with for-each throws ConcurrentModificationException -- use a collection view instead.
map.values().removeIf(v -> ...) removes every entry whose value matches; compare with Objects.equals.
